smoking_behavior.quit_intention: Will quit in the next month

rated_messages.input_message: Practice going 10 minutes without smoking. Think of it just as practice. When the urge passes, reward yourself with a break from work or dinner from your favorite restaurant!
Try to avoid seeing other people smoke. It might sound basic but brain see, brain want! If you can, make life easier and avoid the people you used to smoke with for some time where possible.
Stop! Breathe. What is going on around you? Inside you? Allow everything to be just as it is. Breathe again.
It's normal to have some doubts during a quit attempt. Keep your quit reasons on hand to remind yourself if ever you feel uncertain or undecided.
Picture the people or things you care deeply about. On a scale of 0-10, how willing are you to let this urge pass for those reasons?
Just because other people are smoking, doesn't mean you have to. Practice allowing this urge to be present for 5 minutes. When it passes, give yourself credit.

Read this rule out loud (if you can): IF someone offers me a cigarette THEN I will say 'no thanks, I don't want one.' Reading out if/then rules has been shown to help people stick with their decisions.

Think about your hero, or someone you admire. What do you admire about them? Often our heroes are people who struggle and succeed in difficult circumstances. Now's the chance to be your own hero - by not smoking despite the challenges of stress and strong urges!
Some people find that having a simple mantra can really help, especially if things feel stressful. Try repeating something simple to yourself like: "I can do it!".
Notice how stress and anxiety may pull you and make you want to smoke. Just notice this. You can choose to just notice and not smoke.
